cohort: The study included 75 participants, categorized into early preterm (n=15), late preterm (n=15), term delivery (n=30), and nonpregnant control (n=15) groups.
finding: Elevated maternal serum and placental asprosin levels are significantly linked to preterm birth, showing inverse associations with gestational duration and infant birth weight.
cross-section timing: Serum samples were collected from all individuals, and placental tissues were obtained postdelivery from pregnant participants.
birth_weight: Neonatal birth weight was measured and found to be inversely correlated with serum asprosin (r = -0.683, p = 0.01).
gest_age: Gestational age ranged from before 34 weeks (early preterm) to 37-42 weeks (term delivery), with significant inverse correlations identified between asprosin levels and gestational age.
